lastCommit.message:
OTA-1843 — who the Fallen was

OTA-1362 put `origin.player` on every foreign corpse. Eleven OTAs later, not one
player-facing sentence said it.

The emergence beat, the Arbiter's identification, the enemy's own flavor, the
defeat lines, the reclaim reward — every one of them named the character, the
ground they fell on, their epitaph and their kill count, and NONE of them named
the person whose game they came out of. A Hollowed a friend sent across read
exactly like one grown from your own dead. The single fact the whole mechanic
exists for — THIS WAS ANOTHER REAL PLAYER'S CHARACTER — was the one fact the
game kept to itself.

⚠ NOTHING HERE READS A FIELD THAT WAS NOT ALREADY THERE. These are the same
records, finally saying out loud what they hold. No schema change, no migration.

THE ENCOUNTER. A signature leads the beats and only for a foreign corpse:
"☗ ONE OF THE FALLEN — <name> child of <house>. This one walked in another
player's world before it walked in yours." The Arbiter's identification carries
the house too, because a banner can be scrolled past and the identification is
the beat that says what you are fighting. The enemy's flavor gains one clause.
Your own dead gain nothing — their lines are byte-identical to what shipped,
and the suite asserts that character for character.

⚠ NO CRYPTOGRAPHIC STATE IN COMBAT. Seal, key, verified/legacy — none of it
appears in a single line the mud prints. Those words belong to the exchange
screen. Out here the only question is whose name is on it.

THE BLADE. A reclaimed piece now says whose hand it was in, written into
`description` — a field the item model already had and already persists. Which
forced the real question: two Legendary swords of the same name off two
different corpses are not one sword, and before this they merged into one row
and one of the two names was simply gone. A reclaimed piece is tagged `fallen`
and `inventory.stackCompatible` treats that tag as per-instance, exactly as it
already treats a coating or a rolled stat. It lives there and not beside the
reclaim because OTA-1737 made that function the one authority on "are these the
same kind of thing", and a second opinion is exactly what that OTA removed.

⚠ THE FIRST CUT OF THAT RULE WAS WRONG AND THE FULL SURFACE CAUGHT IT. It read
"descriptions differ → never merge", with a comment asserting that could only
split a stack that was already lying about its contents. It could not. OTA-958's
torch proves it: a starting Aetheric Torch carries its catalog description and
one taken off a tile does not, so the same object in two rows stopped stacking
and `take` looked like it granted twice. OTA-1737 had already written down this
exact hazard about the tag set, measured on that same suite. The marker tag is
the test now, and nothing that stacked yesterday changes.

THE CLOSURE. Defeat IS the rest here — the store writes the rest record on the
same beat it prints the closing lines — so that beat is the only moment the
player has to understand that another person is about to be told their
character's story ended. It now says so, and says what will be sent: who put
them down, where the ground closed, that it is finished. Null for your own dead,
because nothing travels and promising a word to a house that does not exist
would make the transcript a liar.

ARRIVAL AND THE ROLL. Taking a payload in used to report counts. It now reads as
what it is — "<name> child of <house> walk your wastes now. They died in another
player's world and the mud here has them. You will meet them." And the exchange
screen grew THE ROLL: who is still walking, and the last 25 closings. Read-only,
off the ledger the exchange already writes. No new key, no new record.

⚠ WHAT IS NOT THERE, AND WHY. "Encountered" and "defeated" are absent from the
roll on purpose: nothing durable distinguishes them from "rested", because
defeat IS the rest. A row for either would duplicate what is shown or need a new
persisted counter. Deferred rather than faked.

⚠ NO FARMING. A foreign corpse still yields its weapon and an EMPTY armour pool
— OTA-1362's faucet limit, re-asserted here because a "make Fallen feel good"
pass is exactly the pass that would quietly open it. No coin, no XP, no second
reward path, and the Hollowed is still a one-time event. The identity is the
reward.

THE STORE CEILING SHAPED THE ARCHITECTURE, CORRECTLY. The first cut added 27
lines to a file with zero headroom. Its rule — "the responsibility belongs in a
module outside the file" — is the right one: deciding which lines print, on
which channel, in what order is presentation and belongs next to the sentences.
`revenantArrivalLog` and `revenantRestLog` now own that, all three store sites
are SHORTER than they were, and the hook-spawn route gained a signature it never
had, because there is one authority instead of three hand-ordered copies.

Validation: new suite ota1843WhoTheFallenWas 31/31, with a negative twin for
every claim (ordinary enemy, your own dead, ordinary stacking); Fallen and
inventory regressions 262/262; four negative controls red then restored
hash-clean — NC-A initially passed because the house still arrived via the
Arbiter, so the signature-specific test was verified to catch it rather than
assumed; typecheck at the 181 baseline; 25/25 local gates.

Security and exchange untouched: the seal, the pairing and the acceptance gate
carry no OTA-1843 marker, and the admitted/turned-away table is re-asserted.
This pass begins after a corpse is already accepted.
